title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
excerpt: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. title: HeLM: Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory for Non-Markovian Manipulation
excerpt: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have enabled fine manipulation capabilities, yet performing tasks that require working memory remains a key challenge. Most existing VLA architectures operate under a Markovian assumption, mapping only the current observation to an action, which leads to failure in non-Markovian environments. Inspired by the human 'inner monologue', we propose Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory (HeLM), a hierarchical VLA framework that maintains task-relevant history in explicit language through factorized event detection and event-triggered memory updates. ai.summary: HeLM is a hierarchical Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework that uses explicit language memory to handle non-Markovian manipulation tasks, addressing the limitation of standard VLA models that rely on Markovian assumptions.

title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
excerpt: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. ai.summary: The paper introduces Gated DeltaNet‑2 (GDN‑2), a linear‑time attention architecture that uses channel‑wise decay and separate erase/write gates, showing that write operations dominate state updates while erasures have limited impact.
ai.why: GDN‑2 offers constant‑memory inference, enabling developers to build longer‑context language models without quadratic cost.

title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing

We introduce TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn robustness while retaining the generative and editing capabilities acquired through earlier training. title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
excerpt: Autoregressive approaches with large language models, such as long chain-of-thought reasoning, have become the default for new AI applications because they reach higher accuracy on a wide range of tasks. In production, however, they give inconsistent answers, require parsing of outputs, and add cost and latency. Decision models address this: given a question and a set of options supplied by the user, they return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. excerpt: Benchmark compression reduces the often prohibitive time and cost of model evaluation by evaluating models on a small benchmark subset that closely matches full-benchmark results.
